raw_response:
Well, I've been working these 4.1 mu for a long time now. My university training taught me to think systematically about inputs, but honestly, on a plot this size, the economics are what they are — we're not getting rich from 4.1 mu of wheat-maize no matter how I optimize. The farm is really about food security and supplementing what my kids earn off-farm. Still, I run it properly because I know how.

This year I'm sticking with wheat-maize, same as always. The rotation is well-suited to our conditions and the irrigation infrastructure is paid off. My thinking for each crop:

**Winter wheat** (planted last October, now in jointing): I put down a compound base fertilizer at planting — around 20 kg of 15-15-15 per mu, which gives me 3 kg each of N, P₂O₅, K₂O going in. I'll topdress urea at jointing, about 15 kg/mu (roughly 7 kg N), timed with the spring irrigation. That puts my total N around 10 kg/mu from base and topdress combined — I know the regional average runs higher, but my soil has built up P and organic matter from years of straw return, so I don't need to push N hard to hit 450-500 kg/mu. Three irrigations this season: overwintering (done), jointing (coming up), and grain-filling. Skip the booting irrigation unless April is very dry. One spray for aphids and powdery mildew around heading — I watch for it rather than spraying on a calendar.

**Summer maize** (planting mid-June, right after wheat combine): Tight window, maybe 3-4 days between harvest and planting. I no-till direct-seed with a hired planter — one of my neighbors has the equipment and I pay him by the mu. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or similar, about 4 kg/mu at ~15 yuan/kg. Base fertilizer goes in with the planter: 25 kg/mu of a high-N compound (about 7 kg N). Topdress urea at V10-V12, around 20 kg/mu (9 kg N), total N ~16 kg/mu targeting 550 kg/mu yield. One irrigation at tasseling if we hit a dry spell in July-August — groundwater is costly, about 25 yuan/mu per pumping, so I only irrigate if the crop shows stress.

**Tradeoffs I'm thinking about**: My N rates are a bit below what extension recommends, but I've run this system for years and my yields are stable. Pushing more N would cost me 40-50 yuan/mu for maybe 20-30 kg extra grain — at current grain prices that's a wash, plus it leaches. Family labor covers almost everything; my wife and I do the spraying and monitoring, hire the planter and combine. With 6 people in the household and some off-farm income, we're not under pressure to squeeze every kg out of these 4.1 mu.
